Pressure inside a soap bubble = Patm+4γ/R (two surfaces). End1 has a hemispherical bubble with R=r, End2 a sub‑hemispherical cap with the same base radius r but larger radius of curvature R>r, so ΔP1>ΔP2. Hence air flows from end1 to end2. To eliminate the pressure difference the bubble at end1 must lose volume (shrink) and the bubble at end2 must gain volume (expand). Thus option B is correct.
